analysis: The question asks which condition is NOT associated with defects in DNA repair. Fanconi anemia, Li-Fraumeni syndrome, Bloom syndrome, and Xeroderma pigmentosa are all known to involve defects in DNA repair mechanisms. Fanconi anemia involves chromosomal instability due to DNA repair issues. Li-Fraumeni syndrome is associated with mutations in the TP53 gene, which plays a role in DNA repair and cell cycle regulation. Bloom syndrome involves mutations in the BLM gene, affecting DNA repair processes. Xeroderma pigmentosa is characterized by defects in nucleotide excision repair, leading to increased sensitivity to UV light. In contrast, sickle-cell anemia is caused by a point mutation in the hemoglobin gene, resulting in abnormal hemoglobin structure and function, but it is not related to DNA repair defects. Therefore, sickle-cell anemia is the condition that is not associated with defects in DNA repair.
